title: Mac vs NVIDIA — Direct Quantified Comparison
description: This is NOT two separate analyses — this is a DIRECT HEAD-TO-HEAD comparison between Mac Studio (M2 Ultra / M3 Ultra with 192GB unified memory) and the best NVIDIA options (RTX 4090 24GB, RTX 5090 24GB). The comparison must be quantified with numbers, not qualitative statements. Compare across: (1) Effective VRAM for 35B models: Mac's 192GB unified memory vs NVIDIA's 24GB — what does this mean for context length? (Mac can do 128K+ context easily; NVIDIA is limited by 24GB), (2) Memory bandwidth: M2 Ultra (819 GB/s) / M3 Ultra (estimated 1 TB/s) vs RTX 4090 (1008 GB/s) vs RTX 5090 (estimated 1300+ GB/s) — how does this affect token/s? (Mac has higher bandwidth but slower compute per watt), (3) Inference speed: direct comparison of token/s for the SAME 35B model on Mac (MLX) vs NVIDIA (llama.cpp/vLLM) — collect or measure actual numbers, (4) Fine-tuning capability: Mac can load entire model + dataset in memory; NVIDIA requires QLoRA — compare quality and speed, (5) Software ecosystem: MLX vs CUDA — framework maturity, model availability, ease of use, (6) Price: Mac Studio Ultra ($3000-8000+) vs NVIDIA GPU ($1600-2000) + separate CPU/RAM/motherboard, (7) Total cost of ownership: Mac is a complete system; NVIDIA requires building a PC, (8) Longevity: Mac stays useful longer due to unified memory; NVIDIA may become VRAM-limited sooner, (9) Resale value: Mac retains value better, (10) Specific workload scenarios where Mac wins and where NVIDIA wins — with numbers. Every claim must be backed by at least 2 sources or direct measurement.
outputs: direct head-to-head comparison table with numbers
scenario-based verdict: when to choose Mac vs NVIDIA
quantified score for each dimension (1-10 scale)
